Memecylon megacarpum, along with M. excelsum, is one of the most commonly encountered species that have large conspicuously veined leaves and terete or grooved twigs (not conspicuously winged)

However, there is a lot of overlapping variation in leaf size and shape in both these species, and the best way to distinguish M. megacarpum in Peninsular Malaysia is by the raised or flattened midrib

The large, globose, sessile fruit is a reliable character
The leaf margin of M. megacarpum also curls under on drying much more noticeably than in other species, especially near the base
The type of this name is from Sarawak, and was first applied to Peninsular Malaysian collections by Maxwell (1980)
The Bornean material has larger leaves with a sunken midrib above; further work is required to see if the Peninsular Malaysian material represents a new taxon.

Vegetatively easily confused with M. corticosum var. corticosum, as both have winged branches and similar leaf shapes with distinct venation
Memecylon corticosum var. corticosum has slightly thinner leaves that tend to be more elliptic and not as broad towards the base as those of M. wallichii, nor quite as cordate
The midrib in M. wallichii usually dries darker than the lamina beneath; in M. corticosum var. corticosum it is usually paler or concolorous
Memecylon wallichii flowers on leafy internodes (with a distinct woody peduncle), often at or near the tip, whereas M. corticosum var. corticosum is usually ramiflorus (peduncle reduced to a callus)
The anthers of M. wallichii are also unique and distinguish it from all other species in the region
Memecylon excelsum when sterile can be distinguished by the lack of prominent wings, though take care with mature specimens of M. wallichii; the former also has elliptic (not globose) fruits

The leaves of M. paniculatum, which also have winged Twigs, tend to be widest in the middle, as opposed to M. wallichii and M. corticosum var. corticosum which are widest in the bottom third of the lamina; as the name suggests M. paniculatum also has much longer inflorescences
